title: What the cabin tells you
target: What the inside of a Supermarket Simulator vehicle is made of and what it reports, so a delivery run is driven from the dashboard rather than from guesswork.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)

steps.do: Treat the dashboard as part of the car rather than as a separate screen.
steps.because: the dashboard is an object inside the car rather than a screen of its own (DashboardInsideCar)

steps.do: Steer with the vehicle's own steering controls, and expect a limit.
steps.because: steering has its own controls, its own wheel element and a steering limit (SteerWheelControls, SteerWheelUI, SteerConfig, maxSteer)

steps.do: Read your speed rather than feeling for it.
steps.because: the game keeps a speedometer with a current speed and a maximum speed for the vehicle (Speedometer, currentSpeed, maxSpeed)

steps.do: Use the handbrake as its own control, not as a brake you hold.
steps.because: a handbrake is modelled as a control of its own (handBrake)

steps.do: Act on the low-fuel warning when it comes rather than when the engine stops.
steps.because: the game carries a low-fuel warning of its own (RumbleLowFuelWarning)

steps.do: Expect the dashboard to have warning icons of its own.
steps.because: the game ships its own dashboard warning icons, covering the engine among other things (dashboard warning icons)

steps.do: Know that the car itself is built from named parts, not one model.
steps.because: a vehicle has a controller of its own with a separate one for the car, a type, an engine configuration and wheels of its own (VehicleController, CarController, VehicleType, EngineConfig, Wheel)

steps.do: Remember the lights are a system rather than a switch.
steps.because: there is a lighting component, a kind of light and a controller that drives them (CarLighting, CarLightType, VehicleLightController)

commonMistakes: Driving by feel while the speedometer is in front of you.
Treating the handbrake as an ordinary brake.
Ignoring the low-fuel warning until the vehicle stops.
Reading the car's lights as one switch when they are a system.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
